question: Can a projectile weapon fire another family output (a beam) while keeping its own weapon?

routes.reference_swap: A ProjectileType reference cannot name a BeamType (AttackOutputCapabilities).
routes.component_composition: Clone or attach the donor output component to the host entity.
routes.event_action: Suppress the host output on firing and emit the donor output from an event action.

blockers.detail: The Liberator component list (23 components) is followed immediately by the next entity list; all 1909 lists are packed with zero slack, so adding a BeamWeaponComponent overwrites another entity.
BeamWeaponComponentData is a 46-row hash index (23 used, 24 records); a new membership needs a hashed row and a record, and no safe allocation for either exists.
The trigger dispatch routes a weapon with the projectile flag to its projectile trigger and never to its beam trigger, so a Liberator owning both would still fire bullets.
A beam is the firing flag of an entity own beam_weapon instance; there is no request taking a beam type, origin or direction, and the call writes out of bounds for an entity without a beam instance.
Events are polled after the game has fired (player_fired from the stats table, 10 Hz); native output cannot be suppressed without a code hook.
A ProjectileType reference cannot name a BeamType (research/attack-outputs): INCOMPATIBLE_OUTPUT_FAMILY.

beamLifecycle.start: the wielder trigger sets the beam instance firing flag
beamLifecycle.continuous: LAS-5 and LAS-98 (BeamFireMode 4) beam while the flag is set; the Trident (BeamFireMode 6) fires its pulse per trigger (research/attack-outputs)
beamLifecycle.heat: the owner WeaponHeat instance (or, on the 40-K Meltagun, its magazine and charge)
beamLifecycle.networking: not traced; the beam instance belongs to the owner entity
